source_text: Gratias autem Deo, quod fuistis - inquit - servi peccati; sed oboedistis ex corde in eam formam doctrinae, in quam traditi estis; liberati autem a peccato servi estis facti iustitiae [n396] .
pass_a_gloss: But thanks to God, that you were, he says, slaves of sin; but you obeyed from the heart unto that form of doctrine into which you have been handed over; but freed from sin you have been made slaves of justice.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS forma; Blaise Adam forma futuri

pass_b_english: ‘But thanks be to God,’ he says, ‘that you were slaves of sin, but obeyed from the heart the pattern of teaching to which you were entrusted. Freed from sin, you have become slaves of righteousness’ (Romans 6:17–18).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
